claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 requires processing temperatures above 2300 °C.
The equiatomic composition (Hf0.2Zr0.2Ta0.2Nb0.2Ti0.2)B2 is a high-entropy diboride.
Introducing HfB2, TaB2, NbB2, and TiB2 into ZrB2 produces a single-phase, chemically disordered diboride microstructure.
The high-entropy diboride can be densified by spark plasma sintering at approximately 1700–1800 °C.
High-entropy alloying promotes lower-temperature densification relative to single-phase ZrB2.
The high-entropy diboride forms a complex multicomponent oxide scale at high temperature.
Increased configurational entropy lowers the sintering activation energy.
Lower sintering activation energy permits densification at reduced processing temperature.
Chemical disorder in the high-entropy diboride lattice hinders oxygen diffusion.
Chemical disorder in the high-entropy diboride lattice hinders metal-cation diffusion.
Restricted oxygen and cation diffusion produces a protective multicomponent oxide scale.
The equiatomic high-entropy diboride has better oxidation resistance than ZrB2 processed by the same procedure.
The high-entropy diboride can maintain its shape during oxidation exposure at 1500 °C.
A high-entropy diboride fabricated at 1700–1800 °C will have at least comparable mechanical strength to ZrB2 fabricated above 2300 °C.
A high-entropy diboride fabricated at 1700–1800 °C will have at least comparable structural integrity to conventional and lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens.
The high-entropy diboride will have lower corrosion rates in a liquid plating-metal bath than conventional and lower-temperature ZrB2.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens processed at approximately 1700 °C have poorer oxidation resistance than conventional ZrB2.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 specimens processed at approximately 1700 °C have poorer liquid-metal corrosion resistance than conventional ZrB2.
The proposed material is applicable in service at temperatures up to approximately 1500 °C.
The proposed material is applicable to prolonged exposure in liquid plating-metal environments.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires mechanical strength only to be at least comparable to high-temperature ZrB2, whereas the falsification rule requires a statistically significant improvement in mechanical strength; an outcome allowed by the prediction could therefore be declared falsifying.
